text: Helmut Lang, born on 10 March 1956, is an Austrian artist and former fashion designer and mentor who lives and works in New York and on Long Island. In 1986, he presented his first Helmut Lang runway collection in Paris at Centre Georges Pompidou; his first Helmut men's collection debuted in 1987, and a decade later he relocated his label from Vienna to New York. Lang utilized unconventional materials such as rubber, feathers, and metallic fabrics, redefining the silhouette of the 1990s and early 2000s. He broke from the opulent runway show traditions of the 1980s by becoming the first designer to stream his collection online in 1998. His brand was recognized for its utilitarian, minimalist aesthetic and its prestigious denim line. In 1999, Lang sold a 51% stake in his company to the Prada Group, which managed distribution and manufacturing, while Lang retained control of design and advertising. Prada subsequently launched Helmut Lang accessories like shoes, belts, and bags and opened Helmut Lang stores in Hong Kong and Singapore. Sales under the Prada Group declined from $100 million in 1999 to $37 million in 2003, with the cancellation of licensing for external companies to manufacture and market the profitable Helmut Lang Jeans cited as a key reason for the drop in revenue. In 2005, Lang left the label and retired from fashion, after which he has resided in New York City and on Long Island as a practicing artist. In 2006, Prada sold the Helmut Lang brand to Link Theory Holdings. Lang has collaborated with artists Jenny Holzer and Louise Bourgeois, and his recent artistic works explore abstract sculptural forms and physical arrangements beyond the human body. He held his first solo art exhibition, ALLES GLEICH SCHWER, at the Kestnergesellschaft in Hannover in 2008 and has since presented solo exhibitions internationally. Excerpts from his art projects, Long Island Diaries and The Selective Memory Series, have been published in various publications including Purple, BUTT Magazine, Fanzine 137, Visionaire, and most recently The Travel Almanac. The original Helmut Lang stores, all designed by Lang in collaboration with Gluckman Mayner Architects of New York, have been closed; the last to close was the Paris location in late 2005. Four scents created by Lang in cooperation with Procter & Gamble were discontinued with the 2005 closure of the brand. This timeline covers Helmut Lang's work in fashion and art up to 2021.
